# Future Outlook

## Licensing and Openness

- Mojo is developed by Modular Inc. and is currently proprietary: source-available
  but not open source
- this creates a vendor dependency risk for HPC adoption, as institutions may be
  reluctant to build workflows around a closed language
- in contrast, the alternatives discussed in prior work (SYCL, Kokkos, Julia) are
  all fully open source with active community governance
- Godoy et al. note "the promise of becoming open-source by 2026"
  [@godoyMojoMLIRBasedPerformancePortable2025], which could accelerate adoption
  significantly if realised

## Maturity

- Mojo is still pre-1.0. The language specification, standard library, and GPU
  backend are under active development and subject to breaking changes
- features critical for HPC such as multi-node support, MPI interoperability, and
  broader hardware targets beyond NVIDIA are not yet mature or are absent entirely

## Looking Ahead

- a maturing ecosystem including a package manager, debugger tooling, and broader
  MLIR dialect support would reduce the friction that currently makes Mojo a
  research interest rather than a production choice
- the MLIR foundation gives Mojo a structural advantage: adding support for a new
  hardware target reduces to writing a new lowering dialect, which is cheaper than
  the library-level rewrites required by SYCL or Kokkos
- the open question is whether the ecosystem and governance will catch up to the
  technical promise
